# solid-drift

> `solid-drift` is a signal-native animation library for SolidJS: zero dependencies, SSR-safe, and respectful of `prefers-reduced-motion`. One shared `requestAnimationFrame` clock drives every animation in the app.

## Install

```bash
npm install solid-drift
```

```ts
import { createSpring } from "solid-drift";
```

Import from the package root only. Never deep-import from `solid-drift/dist`.

## API

Signal-native: primitives return signals you bind with `style={{ transform: x() }}`. One shared requestAnimationFrame clock drives everything. SSR-safe. Respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

### Core

`createSpring`, `createTween`, `animate`, `drift`, `springPresets`, `createStagger`, `createTimeline`

### Scroll

`createScrollProgress`, `createHorizontalScroll`, `createScrub`, `createScrollColor`, `createScrollTracking`, `createScrollLine`, `createInView`

## Rules

- Every primitive is SSR-safe: on the server, animations do not run and signals hold their final or initial static value.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, motion primitives jump to their end state.
- `createBeat` keeps ticking under reduced motion; callbacks decide what that means visually..
- Test with fake timers and a stubbed `requestAnimationFrame`; keep the rAF queue module-level and never clear it between tests, or the shared engine strands..
- Do not animate layout properties (`width`, `top`, `left`).
- Do not create your own `requestAnimationFrame` loops.
- Do not write your own text splitter.
- Do not pass a new options object on every render to a primitive created once; create the primitive once and drive it through signals..
- Do not deep-import from `solid-drift/dist`.

## Full docs

- SKILL.md in this repo: full API descriptions, recipes, DriftSpec format.
- README.md: per-primitive docs with examples.
- docs/: family guides, recipes, migration, comparison.
